This is how I mulch:

(Mind you mulch holds more moisture for longer than soil so you gotta somewhat understand how your plot holds water)

I prepare the soil first. I usually till after fertilizer to spread nutrients deeper into the soil. If all the nutrients are sitting on the top, plants will form shallow roots.

Instead of raised rows, I use raised mounds. I'm two lazy to thin out and transplant seedlings. I make raised mounds spaced about 1 foot (30cm) apart. I put 3-5 seeds in the mound usually. Then I surrond the mounds with mulch and leave just a small spot on top for seedling to sprout. Now I only have a very small area to keep weed free at the base of my plants.

If there are any trees on the property, try use leaf litter as mulch. It blocks growth better that wood chips but you don't get a moisture holding bonus. You do get a warmth bonus though if you trying to winter some root crops.
